mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.5% signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days during monetary easing cycles.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where FEDFUNDS remains below 0.5% over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% signals aggressive monetary tightening that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods where FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5.0% and increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200k signals a tight labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days through labor market strength interaction.
failure_condition: The joint effect of UNRATE falling below 5.0% and PAYEMS rising above 200k fails to produce positive 60-day SPX returns in more than 55% of instances over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions marked by elevated residential construction (HOUST) above 1700 and robust consumer demand (RSAFS) above 550000, the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns due to valuation compression and policy tightening expectations over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods where HOUST exceeds 1700 and RSAFS exceeds 550000 over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 (relative to 2017=100) signals manufacturing sector weakness that reduces corporate earnings growth expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods where INDPRO falls below 100 over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained INDPRO level above 100 (relative to 2017=100) indicates expanding manufacturing output that supports corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days during expansionary manufacturing regimes.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where INDPRO exceeds 100 over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.5% signals labor market deterioration that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods where UNRATE exceeds 5.5% over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During high inflation (CPIAUCSL above 3.5%) with accommodative policy (FEDFUNDS below 1.0%), the S&P 500 underperforms due to heightened risk of aggressive monetary tightening, leading to negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods where CPIAUCSL > 3.5 and FEDFUNDS < 1.0 over a 5-year rolling window.
